title.value: Optimal control of network-coupled subsystems: Spectral decomposition and low-dimensional solutions
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the main focus of the paper, which is to investigate optimal control of network-coupled subsystems using spectral decomposition for achieving low-dimensional solutions.
title.quote: Optimal control of network-coupled subsystems: Spectral decomposition and low-dimensional solutions

extractions.description: This paper explores the optimal control of network-coupled subsystems by employing spectral decomposition. The method decomposes a complex system into simpler components, allowing for scalable and efficient implementation of control laws. The framework is applicable to systems where dynamics and cost couplings are defined by an underlying graph, and it particularly benefits large-scale network systems by reducing computational complexity. The paper also extends its framework to stochastic systems and discusses applications such as consensus problems in networked control.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any of the predefined eco-responsible categories like Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation, etc. It focuses on control systems and optimization for networked structures, which while potentially useful in applications, does not directly fall into the eco-responsibility categories listed.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we investigate optimal control of network-coupled subsystems where the dynamics and the cost couplings depend on an underlying undirected weighted graph.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the primary category is 'N/A', the sub-category is also marked as 'N/A'. The paper is focused on control systems for network optimization and does not fit the eco-responsible sub-categories provided.
primary_sub_category.quote: The graph coupling matrix in the dynamics may be the adjacency matrix, the Laplacian matrix, or any other symmetric matrix corresponding to the underlying graph.

new_primary_category.quote: A salient feature of the result is that the solution complexity depends on the number of distinct eigenvalues of the coupling matrix rather than the size of the network.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: We use the spectral decomposition of the graph coupling matrix to decompose the overall system into (L + 1) systems with decoupled dynamics and cost.
